name: South Indian Current
scope: Declared 70 E to 90 E eastern-name-convention regional reach. The west gate follows the later convention reserving South Indian Ocean Current for flow beyond the Agulhas Return Current near 70 E; the east gate is the approximate recirculation/splitting region described in historical hydrography. These are selected regional gates, not whole-current endpoints. Western Agulhas Return, northward recirculation, northeastern Australia continuation and ACC paths are not added. All route latitudes and connecting vertices are editorial.
layer: Historical upper-1000 m geostrophic transport context, not a uniform-depth velocity axis or surface trajectory. Variable deep reference surfaces affect diagnosed transport; no layer-specific centerline reconstructed.
time_convention: Editorial regional connection informed by historical hydrographic mean-flow context and source naming conventions. Not a simultaneous observation, monthly climatological axis or annual geometry.
source_locator: Stramma and Lutjeharms (1997), section 3.2 / journal p. 5523 and Figure 7 caption: 90 E recirculation/split and upper-1000 m flow schematic. Later Grand et al. (2015), regional circulation discussion, journal p. 113: SIOC name beyond 70 E. Near-40 S context from Stramma (1992) publisher abstract; drawn latitudes are editorial.
source_citation: Stramma and Lutjeharms (1997), The flow field of the subtropical gyre of the South Indian Ocean, JGR 102, 5513–5530, doi:10.1029/96JC03455.
source_license: Published articles cited for paraphrased facts and naming conventions; no source images, fields or schematic curves copied.
coordinate_selection: OSW holds the selected longitude gates at 70 E and 90 E, using a nominal near-40 S connection with five-degree waypoints. Latitude bands and endpoint offsets are finite editorial sensitivities. No figure digitization, velocity-axis extraction or physical naming junction inferred.
